beats.say: Hello! Today we learn to spot infostealers, programs that hide inside free software.
In just two months, three hundred ninety four thousand computers infected with one such program were found.

visual.label: infected computers found in two months

beats.say: It arrives as free software, a game mod or an activator, and takes passwords, cards and sessions.
The rule is simple: install software only from the official source or through technical support.

scenes.prompt: Find the warning signs in this post.

body.text: SenedYaz Pro 2026, full version, with activator, FREE
Turn off your antivirus before installing, or it will show a false warning.
12,400 people downloaded it, everyone is happy!

spots.label: Paid software for free
spots.explain: A free full version of paid software is the most common bait. The activator itself is often the malware.

spots.label: Not the official site
spots.explain: This is not the software's official site. Nobody knows who put the file there.

spots.label: Password-protected archive
spots.explain: Antivirus cannot look inside a password-protected archive. That is exactly why criminals add a password.

spots.label: Turn off antivirus
spots.explain: A program that wants protection turned off is afraid of it. This is the clearest signal.

spots.label: Made-up numbers
spots.explain: Anyone can write any number in a channel. A download count is no proof of safety.

scenes.title: The home computer
scenes.intro: Your family uses this computer, and you use it for work mail. Decide at every step.

steps.say: The archive from the channel is already downloaded.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: Correct. Deleting a file like this is the safest step, get the software the official way.

actions.label: Open and run
actions.feedback: As soon as the activator runs, it sends passwords and sessions out within seconds. Antivirus may notice too late.

actions.label: Scan with antivirus
actions.feedback: Antivirus cannot see inside a password-protected archive. Even if the scan says clean, do not trust this file.

steps.say: Your daughter has downloaded a mod for a game.

actions.label: Open
actions.feedback: This file goes for the browser, not the game. It takes saved passwords and your work mail session.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: Right. Get game add-ons only from the game's official store.

actions.label: Check the official store with your daughter
actions.feedback: Well done. Explaining the reason to a child protects the next time too.

body.text: A program from an unknown publisher was not started.

steps.say: A film site asked you to install a codec to watch the video.

actions.label: Don't run
actions.feedback: Correct. A site that needs a program to play a video is a trap, watch it somewhere else.

actions.label: Run anyway
actions.feedback: The system warned you, but you made the call. Now the installer will try to switch off your protection.

body.text: Video_Kodek_Setup.exe wants to turn off real-time protection.

steps.say: The installer asks for a new permission.

actions.label: Turn off
actions.feedback: Protection is off and the stealer runs freely. Disconnect the computer and tell technical support.

actions.label: Keep protection on
actions.feedback: Good call, but the program has already run. Tell technical support and change your work passwords from another device.

steps.say: Now you sign in to work mail on this computer.

actions.label: Never
actions.feedback: Correct. A work password saved on a family computer is a stealer's first target.

actions.label: Save
actions.feedback: Children install programs on this computer too. A stealer would take the work password saved here first.

question.prompt: You need paid software for work. What is the safest way?

options.label: I ask technical support or the office software centre
options.feedback: Correct. Licensed software is safe and it gets updates.

options.label: I download the version with an activator from a forum
options.feedback: Activators are the most common way to get infected. Your passwords pay for the free software.

options.label: I download a portable version from a file sharing site
options.feedback: You do not know who uploaded the file. A portable version carries the same danger.

scenes.explain: Software comes only from the official source. On a work computer, technical support does the installing.

nodes.text: Can I download this mod? It is free, I just need to switch off the antivirus for a minute.
nodes.speaker: Aysel (your daughter)
nodes.spoken: Can I download this mod? <breath> It is free, I just need to switch off the antivirus for a minute.

choices.label: No. A program that wants protection off is dangerous, let us look in the official store
choices.feedback: Correct. Explaining the reason works better than a ban.

choices.label: All right, but be quick
choices.feedback: A minute is enough. A stealer does its work in seconds.

nodes.text: The store does not have that mod! All my friends download it from a forum.
nodes.speaker: Aysel (your daughter)
nodes.spoken: The store does not have that mod! <short pause> All my friends download it from a forum.

choices.label: My work mail is on this computer too. Let us make you your own account, and only use the official store
choices.feedback: Well done. A separate account and the official store protect both your family and your work.

choices.label: Then just this once
choices.feedback: Once is enough. A stealer takes passwords and sessions in seconds.

nodes.text: The mod did not work. A black window flashed on the screen and closed.

choices.label: I cut the internet, tell technical support and change my work passwords from another device
choices.feedback: Correct. If you act fast, the stolen sessions become useless.

choices.label: Nothing happened, I will delete the mod
choices.feedback: Deleting is not enough, the data is already gone. Change passwords from a clean device and tell technical support.

points: Activators, free full versions and game cheats are the most common bait
Never install a program that asks you to turn off protection
Do not save work passwords on a family computer
